title: Compatible intersections of small enriched cellular slices
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal U$; smallness is relative to it and all Hom sets are small. Colimits mean [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. An infinite cardinal $\kappa$ is regular if unions of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of size less than $\kappa$ have size less than $\kappa$. A category is $\kappa$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms has a cocone. An object is $\kappa$-presentable if its ordinary Hom functor preserves small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Locally $\kappa$-presentable means cocomplete and generated under these colimits by a small family of $\kappa$-presentable objects. Let $\kappa$ be uncountable regular and $\mathcal A$ an ordinary locally $\kappa$-presentable category enriched, tensored and cotensored over small simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set, def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor]. Let $I$ be a small simplicial category with fewer than $\kappa$ objects: its simplicial Hom objects have associative composition and identity vertices. Enriched functors $F:I\to\mathcal A$ have actions $I(i,j)\otimes F_i\to F_j$ satisfying unit and composition laws; enriched transformations commute with these actions as simplicial maps. Assume that each functor $I(i,j)\otimes-:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ takes $\kappa$-presentable objects to $\kappa$-presentable objects.

Let $L$ be any arrow class with $\kappa$-presentable endpoints, and let $f:F\to G$ be an enriched transformation. For each $i$, fix a $\kappa$-good $L$-cellular tree with root $F_i$, small well-founded indexing poset $T_i$, and colimit $G_i$ realizing $f_i$, as in [def-coef-good-cellular-tree]. For downward-closed $B\subseteq T_i$ write $Y_i(B)$ for its colimit in $F_i/\mathcal A$. A slice consists of downward-closed subsets $B_i\subseteq T_i$ and enriched diagram actions on the objects $Y_i(B_i)$ making $F\to Y(B)\to G$ enriched transformations with composite $f$. A slice extends another if its subsets contain the other's and the canonical tree-colimit maps form an enriched transformation. Given a slice $M$ with subsets $A_i$ and subsets $E_i\subseteq T_i$ with $|E_i|<\kappa$, there exist slices $N,N'$ with subsets $B_i$ and $B_i\cap A_i$, respectively, such that $E_i\subseteq B_i$, $|B_i|<\kappa$, and $N'$ extends to both $N$ and $M$. Thus the intersection maps commute with every simplicial action. The roots $F_i$ and the objects $G_i,Y_i(A_i)$ need not be presentable.
